On September 8, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud
held talks in Moscow
.
👉
Opening remarks by Sergey Lavrov
👉
Joint press conference of the Ministers
The Foreign Ministers spoke in favour of maintaining regular political dialogue and expanding exchanges of delegations.
They stressed the need to deepen business cooperation in order to ensure sustained positive momentum in bilateral trade.
❗️
The Ministers conducted a thorough exchange of views on key international and regional issues.
Priority attention was given to the escalation of tensions in the Persian Gulf as a result of
US-Israeli aggression against Iran
.
Sergey Lavrov briefed his Saudi counterpart in detail on
the updated Russian Concept of Collective Security in the Persian Gulf
. He reaffirmed Russia’s readiness for constructive engagement with all interested parties with a view to building a comprehensive security architecture and promoting interstate cooperation in this strategically important region.
The Ministers
expressed mutual concern over rising tensions in the south of the Arabian Peninsula and in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
They noted that the path towards lasting stabilisation in Yemen lies through strict observance of the ceasefire and the earliest possible launch of an inclusive national dialogue involving all of the country’s political forces under UN auspices.
The Sides expressed a shared position in support of preserving Syria’s unity, territorial integrity and sovereignty
. They reaffirmed the need to consolidate international efforts in support of its post-conflict recovery.
Sergey Lavrov outlined Russia’s assessments of the evolving geopolitical situation, including the situation in Ukraine.
He reaffirmed Russia’s commitment to a comprehensive and lasting settlement of the Ukrainian crisis, which can only be achieved through the complete and irreversible elimination of its
root causes
.
#RussiaSaudiArabia

🎙
Remarks and answers to media questions
by Russia's Minister of Foreign Affairs Sergey Lavrov during a joint press conference with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud
(Moscow, September 8, 2026)
Key points
:
🇷🇺
🇸🇦
#RussiaSaudiArabia
: We discussed in detail the key aspects of trade and economic cooperation.
We are pleased that
bilateral trade increased significantly in 2025, by almost 40%
. We share an interest in doing everything possible to sustain this momentum.
•
We reaffirmed our commitment to continued close coordination within OPEC+
in order to maintain a balance between supply and demand on the global energy market. This is particularly important under the current circumstances. As co-chairs of this group of countries, Russia and Saudi Arabia will consistently pursue coordinated approaches.
•
There are good prospects for cooperation in tourism
. Saudi tourists enjoy visiting Russia. In 2025, their number
increased by 35%
compared with the previous year. The number of Russian tourists visiting Saudi Arabia is growing at a similar pace. This has been facilitated by
the Agreement on visa-free travel for our citizens
, which entered into force in May 2026.
•
We discussed the regional agenda, with particular attention to the situation in the Persian Gulf
. We in Russia regret that the countries of the Arabian Peninsula have been drawn, through no choice of their own, into
the military confrontation between the US and Israel on the one hand and Iran on the other
. Together with our Arab partners, we believe that all emerging differences must be resolved
exclusively through
political and diplomatic means
.
•
We paid special attention to the situation in the Palestinian territories, above all in the Gaza Strip
. Unfortunately, despite the existence of an agreement presented as a “plan” by US President Donald Trump, there has been no progress. Both Moscow and Riyadh proceed from the understanding that only
a comprehensive and all-encompassing settlement of
the Palestinian issue
can guarantee lasting peace for all peoples of the region.
•
We noted the importance of ensuring the security and freedom of commercial navigation in all parts of the World Ocean
, including waters adjacent to Yemen.
•
We see the path towards sustainable normalisation in Yemen in the earliest possible launch of direct dialogue among all influential Yemeni political forces
, possibly under UN auspices. At the same time, it is essential to preserve the foundation provided by the “road map” developed at Saudi Arabia’s initiative and agreed with both the internationally recognised authorities of Yemen and representatives of the Ansar Allah movement.

item.title: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's comment on the evacuation of passengers and crew of the Russian vessel Professor Molchanov from the Spitsbergen archipelago
item.description: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's comment on the evacuation of passengers and crew of the Russian vessel Professor Molchanov from the Spitsbergen archipelago (September 8, 2026) 💬 On September 8, a group of passengers and crew members (69 people in total) from the Russian research vessel Professor Molchanov, arrested on September 2 in Spitsbergen at the request of Ukrainian companies, crossed the Russia-Norway border and is now en route to Murmansk. The Russian nationals were evacuated with assistance from the Norwegian authorities through close coordination between State Trust Arktikugol , Embassy of Russia in Oslo and the Russian Consulates General in Spitsbergen and Kirkenes . ☝️ The Russian nationals have received the necessary assistance and support. Following their border crossing, the Murmansk regional authorities are helping arrange their onward journey to Murmansk.

item.title: 🎙 Opening remarks by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov during talks with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud
item.description: 🎙 Opening remarks by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov during talks with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud (Moscow, September 8, 2026) 💬 Sergey Lavrov: We are pleased to welcome you to Moscow. We highly appreciate that, despite the difficult situation in the region, you found the time to come to Moscow. This underscores the special nature of our relations , which are not dependent on the current political climate and are focused on implementing the agreements reached by our Leaders. We particularly value this visit and the opportunity to hold substantive talks , especially given that this year marks the centenary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Russia and Saudi Arabia . This is a good opportunity to take a detailed look at the state of Russia-Saudi relations. They continue to expand year by year in trade and the economy, investment, culture and humanitarian cooperation. We will also discuss regional affairs. 🤝 Russia is sincerely interested in helping advance efforts to calm the situation , as well as in addressing other regional issues of mutual interest. 🇷🇺 🇸🇦 #RussiaSaudiArabia

📃
Article by Their Excellencies Mr Stanislav Krans and Mr Wang Xiaolong, Ambassadors of Russia and China to New Zealand, “Forged in Pain and Fire: WWII History to Defend”, published on
The NZ Herald’s website
(September 4, 2026)
👉
Read in full
• September 3rd marks the 81st Anniversary of the End of World War II.
The Allies’ victory in World War II laid the foundation of the United Nations
that was established in 1945 with the aims, as stipulated at its Charter, “to save succeeding generations from the scourge of war”.
• Nearly 80 percent of the world’s population were drawn into the fiery orbit of hostilities. As the primary theaters of military operations in Europe and Asia, the Soviet Union and China bore the brunt of World War II. Altogether their casualties accounted for over half of the deaths worldwide. Most losses were among civilians who suffered greatly from the Axis powers’ war crimes.
Lest we forget the Chinese and Soviet people’s sacrifice for the victory as well as the contribution of other Allies, including New Zealand, to crushing Nazism and fascism and fighting for a peaceful future!
• During World War II, Japanese militarists’ war of aggression and innumerable crimes inflicted immense suffering on the people of China, Russia and elsewhere across Asia, resulting in the deaths of tens of millions of innocent people
. 80 years have passed, it is painful to see that Japan has not fully reflected on its past crimes.
Instead, shielded and encouraged by outside forces, it now attempts openly to whitewash its aggression and even to return openly to a militarist path.
• Annually, the respective UN General Assembly resolution – sponsored by Russia and co-sponsored by China and 43 other countries
– is supported by the overwhelming majority of member-states
. Last year, 119 nations voted for this document. Unfortunately,
New Zealand is not among them being in the minority, although Kiwis were actively involved in the fight against Nazism
and won fame on the battlefields of World War II.
• Back in the days of World War II, New Zealand and many other nations were on the right side of the history and their cause was just. Russia and China are determined to
stand firmly on the side of international justice and prepared, together with the peace-loving peoples of all nations, to resolutely uphold the post-war world order for the sake of building a bright future for all mankind
.

🎙
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov's
answer to a question
from Andrew Napolitano during an interview with Channel One’s
The Great Game programme
(Moscow, September 8, 2026)
❓
Question: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner recently visited Moscow and met with President of Russia Vladimir Putin. What can you tell us about the outcome of this visit?
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
Much of the opening part of these talks
was broadcast on television
: President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
’s remarks, followed by statements from
Steve Witkoff
and
Jared Kushner
. Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov, who took part in the conversation,
later gave a detailed comment
.
In our diplomatic tradition,
we generally limit ourselves to what we have decided to make public
.
I do not want to emulate
those who are now beginning to speculate
about
“what Mr Witkoff and Mr Kushner brought to Moscow and what they subsequently took to Kiev”
. A member of Ukraine's parliament has already said that what they brought back was far worse than what Ukraine had previously rejected.
❗️
There is a great deal of speculation.
As for further diplomatic steps,
the American Side has said nothing
.
The French, however, have already announced that they were there and that the Americans supposedly said that,
following the elections to Russia's State Duma
, direct talks involving the US would definitely resume.
I leave all of this on the conscience of the Élysée Palace
, especially given that it has repeatedly gained notoriety for
less-than-ethical conduct
when it comes to disclosing the substance of telephone and other conversations.
The substance of what was discussed is based – and I can say this with confidence – on
the position President Donald Trump outlined on Ukraine
immediately after returning to the Oval Office.
☝️
First, he said that
any attempts to draw Ukraine into NATO should simply be forgotten.
He recalled that this had been clear long before President Vladimir Putin, that the matter was closed and there was no reason to try to reopen it.
👉
The second element of the US position is
recognition of the realities on the ground.
I would particularly stress that
this is not about territories
.
When we speak of realities,
we are talking about people
who, immediately after
the February 2014 coup
, were branded “subhuman”, “specimen” and terrorists. When they rejected the results of
the illegal coup
, the army, combat aircraft and artillery were deployed against them – something categorically prohibited under international humanitarian law.
They were simply not treated as human beings.
Shortly after being elected president in 2014, Poroshenko said that their children – the children of “real Ukrainians” – would go to clean schools and kindergartens, while the children of those living in Donbass would rot in basements
.
So how do the Europeans intend to return these people to the rule of that regime when they call for restoring the 1991 borders?
Simply to hand the territory over to Nazis? Or do they want to punish these people for wanting to preserve their freedom, their culture and their belonging to the Russian world?
I have spoken about this
many times
.
I would like to stress that
the realities on the ground
, which President Donald Trump and his team recognise – as far as we can judge, they continue to recognise them, just as they did in Alaska –
are realities connected with people
,
with the views they expressed in referendums
: in Crimea, in the Donetsk and Lugansk People’s Republics and, of course, in the Zaporozhye and Kherson regions.
The fact that the Americans proceed from these realities in all their contacts with us, above all in their contacts with President Vladimir Putin, naturally elicits
a positive response from us and strengthens our readiness to continue talking with them
.

item.description: 🇷🇺 Today, September 8, we mark the Day of the Languages of the Peoples of Russia for the first time. The main goal of the holiday is to preserve and support Russia’s linguistic diversity , promote native languages, and strengthen interethnic harmony and respect for the cultures of all the peoples of our country. Russia fosters more than 150 languages , each of which is an invaluable cultural heritage of the peoples of our nation. *** 🔹 More than 190 peoples live in Russia, each with its own cultural and linguistic traditions. There are more than 270 different languages and dialects in total, which can be divided into several major groups: • Slavic languages. Russian is the state language and the most widely spoken language. • Turkic languages. These include Tatar, Bashkir and Chuvash. • Finno-Ugric languages. These include Mari, Udmurt and Komi. • Caucasian languages. These include Avar, Chechen and Ingush. • Paleoasiatic languages. These include Chukchi and Koryak. 🔹 105 languages are represented in the education system: 24 are used as languages of instruction, while 81 are taught as academic subjects. 🔹 Russian is the state language and the most widely spoken language throughout the country. 🔹 The rarest languages of the peoples of Russia include Itelmen and Copper Island Aleut , each of which has only one competent speaker remaining. 🇷🇺
Today, September 8, we mark
the Day of the Languages of the Peoples of Russia
for the first time.
The main goal of the holiday is to
preserve and support Russia’s linguistic diversity
, promote native languages, and strengthen interethnic harmony and respect for the cultures of all the peoples of our country.
Russia fosters more than
150 languages
, each of which is an
invaluable cultural heritage
of the peoples of our nation.
***
🔹
More than 190 peoples
live in Russia, each with its own cultural and linguistic traditions. There are more than 270 different languages and dialects in total, which can be divided into
several major groups:
• Slavic languages.
Russian is the state language and the most widely spoken language.
• Turkic languages.
These include Tatar, Bashkir and Chuvash.
• Finno-Ugric languages.
These include Mari, Udmurt and Komi.
• Caucasian languages.
These include Avar, Chechen and Ingush.
• Paleoasiatic languages.
These include Chukchi and Koryak.
🔹
105 languages
are represented in the education system: 24 are used as languages of instruction, while 81 are taught as academic subjects.
🔹
Russian is the state language and
the most widely spoken language
throughout the country.
🔹
The rarest languages of the peoples of Russia include
Itelmen and Copper Island Aleut
, each of which has only one competent speaker remaining. Several other languages have
fewer than ten speakers
, including the Orok language on Sakhalin, Negidal and Udege languages in Khabarovsk Krai, Southern Yukaghir in Yakutia, Southern Selkup in Tomsk Region, Votic in Leningrad Region, as well as Kildin Sámi and Akkala Sámi in Murmansk Region.
